title: Why everyone’s talking about Cornell University
description:
The issue of safety on college campuses is nothing new. But it’s back in the spotlight again because of the re-opening of a case at Cornell University, New York in the US. A woman alleges she was gang raped at a fraternity party in October 2024. The group is being called the ‘Cornell 7’ on social media. The incident was reported to campus police at the time, but no formal charges were made.

The woman claims she was drugged and raped at a frat house and says the uni didn’t protect her or adequately punish the men she says were involved. Cornell rejects this. Her lawyer says she was traumatised and dropped out of uni.

Now, two years later, state prosecutors have reopened the investigation following a civil lawsuit she’s filed. So - what happened with the case the first time? And what’s different now?

We speak to the BBC’s New York correspondent Nada Tawfik about the case and the conversations about consent, accountability and campus sexual assault.

If you are affected by any of the issues in this episode, details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide. www.befrienders.org

summaryEn: This episode examines the reopening of a sexual assault investigation involving Cornell University students, dubbed the 'Cornell 7' on social media. A female student, known legally as Jane Doe, alleges she was drugged and gang-raped at a fraternity party in October 2024. While Cornell conducted a Title IX investigation resulting in disciplinary actions, local prosecutors initially declined to file criminal charges. Following a recent civil lawsuit filed by the victim and the emergence of vulgar group Snapchat messages, state prosecutors have reopened the criminal investigation to determine if charges should be presented to a grand jury. The episode highlights ongoing discussions around campus safety, consent, accountability, and the bystander effect.
